items.message: 'Would' can't be used with a state like 'have' — use 'used to'.

After 'Did', it's 'use to' — no '-d' on 'use'.
After 'didn't', it's 'use to' — drop the '-d'.
'Am used to' means 'accustomed to', and 'when I was young' is the past — for a finished past habit, say 'I used to skate'.
'Own' is a state verb — 'would' can't be used. Use 'used to own'.
'Be scared' is a state — 'would' can't be used. Use 'used to be'.
In an affirmative statement, it's 'used to' (with '-d'), not 'use to'.
After 'would', use the base verb: 'would borrow', not 'would borrowed'.
After 'use to', use the base verb: 'play', not 'played'.
After 'use to', use the base verb: 'get', not 'getting'.
'Live' describes a state — use 'used to', not 'would'.
After 'used to', use the base verb: 'visit', not 'visiting'.
After 'use to', use the base verb: 'go', not 'went'.
'Know' is a state verb — this needs 'used to know', not 'would'.
After 'didn't', it's 'use to' — no '-d'.
'Is used to' means 'accustomed to' — a finished past habit needs 'She used to teach'.
'Would' can't be used with a state like 'have a pet' — use 'used to'.
After 'use to', use the base verb: 'work', not 'worked'.
After 'would', use the base verb: 'would sit', not 'would sat'.
